reason: Prioritize the requested n=512-specific unroll: it preserves reduction order and limits code changes to the main workload, though added live vectors create register-pressure risk. Next are small scheduling or loop-control changes with low correctness risk. Pointer advancement has mixed paired results and no stable gain; the n=512 pointer variant also had noisy, inconclusive trials. Transpose changes, packing, scratch changes, and combining streaming regions affect more work or add memory and boundary complexity. The severe regression for the earlier packed-B and streaming-region trials argues for lower priority, but does not establish causality for these distinct proposals. All recommendations remain unverified; retain the incumbent unless fresh paired trials and correctness checks support adoption.
